thread:
incident-bot: @channel HIGH: Smart-routing error spike in prod (service=redwood-api, route=/v1/generate). 5xxs started at 2026-03-15T09:20:34Z. Autosuggest: possible routing/fallback policy loop. Paging @sara @josh @anya :rotating_light:

sara: on it, starting triage. which customers impacted? any recent routing policy changes?

josh: seeing lots of mismatched payload errors in the logs — requests for 'generation' being routed to a 'chat' variant. snippet from logs:
```
2026-03-15T09:21:01Z ERROR routing_engine: variant_mismatch: expected=gen, got=chat model_id=gpt-chat-3b-v2 request_id=abc123
2026-03-15T09:21:02Z WARN fallback: attempting fallback to variant=gpt-instruct-3b-v1
2026-03-15T09:21:02Z ERROR fallback_loop: no_compatible_variant_found, increment=1
```

anya: quick hypothesis: pinned model mapping for the customer tier was updated in last deploy. looks like the pin points at a model tag that resolves to a chat family instead of instruct/gen. that triggers the runtime to try fallbacks across families -> incompatibility loop.

mike: can we temporarily disable smart-routing for affected tenants or override fallback_policy to fail fast? propose run: `redwoodctl routing update --tenant acme --smart-routing off` or flip fallback_policy to `fail_fast` for the route.

sara: doing controlled mitigation now. running command for tenant scope (ACME first):
```
# disable smart routing for ACME tenant
redwoodctl tenants update acme --set smart_routing=false --auth-token $REDWOOD_OPS_TOKEN
```
Output: ok: updated tenant acme (smart_routing=false)

incident-bot: CHANGE: smart-routing disabled for tenant acme by sara at 2026-03-15T09:25:12Z. Monitoring for error rate reduction.

josh: error rate dropped ~85% for acme in the last 3m. global error rate still elevated ~20% because other tenants had the same pin mapping. listing recent deploys to routing-config: `git log --oneline -- routers/* | head` shows a merge from feature/routing-tags at 2026-03-15T08:58Z.

anya: yep that merge added a new tag-to-model resolver that mistakenly resolves ambiguous tag `stable-gen` to a chat build in some regions. cause: tagging mismatch between model registry and onboarding script.

mike: next step: rollback the tag resolver change in staging then production. I'll open a quick revert PR and patch the resolver to validate model family when tag resolves. temporary mitigation for remaining tenants: set a global fallback_policy to `fail_fast` and a safety validation in the router to reject incompatible family mappings. command to set global safety guard:
```
redwoodctl config set global.router.validate_family=true
redwoodctl config set global.router.fallback_policy=fail_fast
```

sara: applied global fallback_policy change at 2026-03-15T09:34:50Z. Confirming reduced cross-tenant noise.

customer-ops-bot: NOTE: customers affected: ACME Corp (500 errors ~1.2k requests), NovaApps (300 errors), internal health checks flagged. Outbound notifications queued for SRE and account teams.

josh: collecting numbers: total failed requests ~1.8k over 18m window. impact window: 09:20:34Z - 09:40:12Z (mitigated for most at 09:25, global at 09:34). no sustained data loss, only request failures.

anya: root cause summary for postmortem: tag resolver accepted tag aliases that do not guarantee family compatibility. race condition in model-registry sync allowed `stable-gen` alias to point to a chat artifact in region eu-west-1. when smart-routing attempted region fallback, the variant family mismatch triggered fallbacks that were not considered compatible -> repeated failure attempts until fail_fast applied.

mike: action items (short-term):
- revert resolver change (PR #4823) by EOD (mike)
- add resolver family validation on tag update (anya)
- add unit/integration tests for tag->model family mapping (josh)
- add automated canary for routing changes (sara)

sara: handing off to next on-call for monitoring and postmortem follow-up. @mike you have the shift, please continue until 10:30Z.

mike: ack, taking over. I'll keep monitoring and start the revert PR now.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated 2026-03-15T09:35:00Z. severity=sev2. follow-up: postmortem required.

josh: quick note for customer comms: suggested wording for ACME: "We experienced a routing misconfiguration causing generation requests to be routed to incompatible model variants, leading to request errors between 09:20–09:34 UTC. We have mitigated the issue and implemented a fix; detailed postmortem forthcoming."

anya: adding one more: postmortem checklist should include timestamps, affected customers, exact model ids involved (do not include internal registry tokens), and the PR that introduced change.

mike: logging the incident in postmortems/ with link to PR and deploys. leaving the thread open for any late alerts.

sara: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
